accuracy.evidence: Definitions checked against the PSHE Association programme of study (KS2: recognise and challenge stereotypes; about discrimination and its impact), DfE Relationships Education guidance 2019 (respect for differences, stereotypes can be unfair) and the Equality Act 2010, whose nine protected characteristics are listed exactly as in section 4. Prejudice is an attitude and discrimination an action, as in EHRC guidance.

misconceptions.evidence: Addresses the common confusions named in the adult text: calling a private feeling discrimination, treating any different treatment as discrimination (Sam missing the try-out, Mo moved for talking), seeing reasonable adjustments such as extra time as unfair, dismissing remarks as 'just a joke', and thinking standing up must mean confronting people.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagprej has mechanics no other lab uses: building a three-box chain idea, feeling, action for two stories; sorting cases by whether the reason is who someone is; tapping concentric ripple rings round one girl to reveal harm; shielding the nine protected characteristics among distractors; and multi-selecting safe responses including an online scene. Shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners build the idea from cases: placing 'Thinks: Travellers steal' in Idea then the distrust in Feeling and the exclusion in Action shows the chain; the reason test explains each card; the rings name the harm to Nadia, her family, other Muslim children and the class; wrong shields (favourite food, football team) are explained as not protected.

predictions.evidence: Locked predictions with tempting distractors: whether Ella's private dislike is discrimination before the chain shows it is prejudice; whether a different treatment is always discrimination before the reason sort; and who is hurt by one unfair act before the ripple rings open outward from Nadia.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with tagged wrong answers: 'act' says nothing was done yet so it is prejudice, 'fair' and 'club' explain why origin or disability are not fair reasons, 'left' says being left out is not always discrimination, 'joke' and 'blame' address hurtful remarks, and 'fight'/'ignore' explain the safer first step.

readability.evidence: Learner audience: validate_lessons passes with kid text at FK 4.2 and adult text at FK 9.1. Kid paragraphs use short named cases (Sam, Priya, a deaf girl); adult text uses exact PSHE terms: stereotype, prejudice, discrimination, protected characteristics, Equality Act 2010, reasonable support.

no_filler.evidence: No filler phrases found by the content gate, and explanation overlap is below the 12 percent limit. Each kid paragraph gives one distinction with a case; adult paragraphs cover curriculum, the term chain and law, named mistakes and the lab sequence.

mobile.evidence: Checked screenshots on Android 360x640 light and dark and iPhone 13 light for every step. Canvas text was 10 to 11 px on 360 px and was raised by 1 to 2 px for slots, tiles, scenarios and notes, then rechecked; tiles in two columns fit and buttons wrap. walk.cjs passes on desktop and iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: axe clean in both themes; all drag actions have equivalent buttons (Idea: stereotype, Discrimination, ring names, each characteristic, each response), the canvas aria-label tracks the spoken note, slot colours carry text labels, and Show me finishes each task within the 6-second limit with no console errors.

sources: PSHE Association (2020) Programme of Study for PSHE Education KS1-5: Living in the Wider World and Relationships (stereotypes, prejudice, discrimination)
DfE (2019) Relationships Education, RSE and Health Education statutory guidance: respectful relationships
Equality Act 2010, section 4 protected characteristics; EHRC guidance for schools
